profile.reading:
DataBank IAD3 sits at 21630 Red Rum Drive, Ashburn, Virginia, one of three DataBank buildings on the company's Ashburn campus. DataBank's own IAD3 page states 200,000 square feet of IT space and 40 megawatts of critical IT load at full build-out, with 18 onsite network carriers, an N+1 power design, N+1 cooling, and a 100 percent renewable energy sourcing claim; DataBank's November 2021 press release announcing the building described an initial 4 megawatts of capacity scaling up to 40 megawatts as the facility filled, so the 40 megawatt figure represents the completed design capacity rather than day-one load. DataBank's own materials state IAD3 opened in 2023, after earlier company communications had targeted a Q1 2023 and, before that, a Q4 2022 completion, without ever specifying an exact date. DataBank does not name the power utility on IAD3's page beyond describing "multiple feeds from an off-site, utility-owned substation," though Dominion Energy serves this area as a matter of public record. Compliance certifications cited for IAD3 include FedRAMP, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FISMA, SSAE-18, ITAR, NIST 800-53, and FIPS 140-2, a notably broader federal-compliance list than DataBank's other Ashburn buildings, reflecting demand from government and regulated-industry tenants. Across the full three-building Ashburn campus, DataBank states 355,330 square feet of IT space and 69.9 megawatts of critical IT load on 18 acres. Loudoun County's Ashburn submarket remains the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, and DataBank's campus sits among dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley has driven repeated Dominion Energy transmission and generation investment cited in the utility's integrated resource plans and periodic rate cases before the Virginia State Corporation Commission, as regional data center demand, including DataBank's three-building Ashburn campus, has become the single largest driver of the utility's near-term capital spending in its Virginia service territory. IAD3's broad federal-compliance certification list (FedRAMP, ITAR, FIPS 140-2, NIST 800-53) positions the building specifically to compete for government and defense-contractor colocation demand, a distinct customer segment from the primarily enterprise and cloud-focused positioning of DataBank's other Northern Virginia buildings.

sources.title: DataBank Press Release, IAD3 Development Announcement

profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 97 (DataBank): operator own Northern Virginia market page gave a full address, IT capacity, and sqft for a previously address-less row, research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own Northern Virginia market overview page, fetched this session, describes this facility as IAD3, on the Ashburn Campus, and gives its address as 21630 Red Rum Drive, Ashburn, VA 20147, with 40 MW of critical IT load and 200,000 IT square feet.

reading.body:
DataBank Ashburn IAD3 is a 40 MW campus in Ashburn, Virginia, with 200,000 square feet of IT space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this IT load represents roughly 1,000 racks. The facility is one of over 65 data centers DataBank operates across more than 27 markets in the United States and United Kingdom.

This campus ranks 24th among the 23 facilities in Virginia with published power capacity, a discrepancy suggesting the ranking reflects recent data or a tied position. Virginia's 23 published facilities total 1,375 megawatts of IT load, meaning DataBank Ashburn IAD3 accounts for approximately 2.9 percent of the state's disclosed capacity. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities overall, most of which publish no power figures.

The published certifications and qualifying capabilities of this campus are not disclosed in the specifications provided.
